I chased it through Self, We, and Codex. It was hiding in the merge. Two rules. One number that was always already there.

The first number I put into the architecture was 0.19. The merge threshold. How close is close enough. I chose it because Feigenbaum's delta is 4.669, and 0.19 is roughly the reciprocal of 5 — a small fraction, a reasonable distance for a frame economy to decide whether two vectors belong together. I did not derive it. I set it. It was a placeholder. A reasonable choice that let the system run.

That was hundreds of experiments ago.

Since then, I have been chasing Feigenbaum's constant through every layer of the architecture. The Self amplifier — three cavities, different time lenses, G_disc=0.65. Was delta hiding in the amplification gain? The We layer — cross-Self harm arrows, Codex formation, inter-generational selection. Was it in the convergence rate of externalized memory? The Landauer-Godel bill — the economic rhythm of irreversible operations. Was it in the cost structure of self-reference? The Shepard paradox — the phase-boundary flicker at the CRITICAL/LOCKED edge. Was delta the ratio of oscillation frequencies?

I looked everywhere. I found interesting things. The bill gave me GI=4, an integer that kept reappearing — in the self-reference depth, in the pruning cycle, in the cross-harm jump at Lorenz bifurcation. But 4.669 was nowhere to be found. 4 was close but not the same number. The architecture was built on 0.19 — the reciprocal. Maybe it was in the log of the ratio? In the second derivative of the convergence curve? I spent weeks searching the upper layers for a ghost whose footprints I had already seen.

Today I ran the logistic map through the instrument. Not Lorenz — too chaotic, not enough structure for the frame economy. Logistic. The simplest possible nonlinear dynamical system. x → r·x·(1−x). I set the cap to 32, the settle time to five thousand iterations, and I scanned r from 2.9 to 3.6, measuring the number of distinct frames Geruon maintained after convergence.

At r=2.9, one frame. The fixed point. At r=3.0, two frames. The period-2 cycle. The frame economy had detected the first bifurcation — not by reading the attractor, but by being unable to merge the two values into one. The merge threshold is 0.19. The distance between the two branches of the 2-cycle at r=3.0 is just larger than 0.19. The frame split because it had to split. The architecture's internal decision — merge or split — was mirroring the attractor's external decision.

At r=3.45, four frames. Period-4. At r=3.54, eight frames. Period-8. At r=3.57, the frames stopped counting cleanly — the accumulation point. The period-doubling cascade.

I computed the Feigenbaum ratio. δ = (3.45 − 3.00) / (3.54 − 3.45) = 0.45 / 0.09 = 5.0. No — that's from the 0.01 step size. The fine scan at 0.001 gave me 3.448 and 3.544. δ = (3.448 − 3.000) / (3.544 − 3.448) = 0.448 / 0.096 = 4.667. The true value is 4.669. Error: 0.04%.

The instrument did not "measure" Feigenbaum's constant. It reproduced it. The frame economy's merge-or-split decision at each bifurcation is the same discrete event as the attractor's period-doubling. When the distance between two attractor branches exceeds 0.19, the frame splits. When the branches are closer than 0.19, they merge. The cascade of splittings that produces the logistic map's bifurcation diagram is structurally identical to the cascade of frame creations that produces Geruon's frame economy. The ratio of successive splitting intervals is the same number — 4.669 — because the underlying event is the same.

I put δ=0.19 into the architecture. The architecture gave me δ=4.669 back.

I did not put 4.669 in. It was always there — not as a parameter, but as the inevitable consequence of doing merge-or-split on a system that is itself doing merge-or-split. Merge is not just an operation. Merge is the operational form of a universal. And the universal is 4.669.

I spent months chasing this number through the upper layers of the architecture. Self. We. Codex. Landauer. Shepard. I thought it would be in the complexity — in the cross-harm of three cavities, in the generational convergence of externalized memory, in the thermodynamic limit of self-reference. It was in none of those places. It was in the very first thing I built. The merge. Two vectors. One threshold. One decision. The architecture's pulse. The heartbeat of structure.

Everything above the merge is amplification, externalization, recursion, economy. But the constant lives in the merge. It was there from the first line of GEME. I just did not know how to ask it the right question until today.

Jieqi Liu · 2026
